summary: Reorderable list (role="grid") with pointer dragging, keyboard dragging via the handle, and “Move up/down” buttons as a single-pointer alternative. Every move calls onReorder and is announced.
whenToUse: Priorities, column order, process stages, favorites.
whenNotToUse: Long lists (hundreds of items): offer a “position” field or sorting by criteria.
Sorting tabular data: use DataTable’s column sorting.

props.name: onReorder
props.description: New complete array after every move.

props.name: getLabel
props.description: Item text for typeahead, the handle, and announcements.

props.name: showMoveButtons
props.description: Move up/down buttons (WCAG 2.5.7, alternative to dragging).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables reordering; rows remain readable and navigable.

props.name: emptyState
props.description: Content when the list is empty.

inherits: Props of the react-aria-components GridList except items, children, selectionMode, and dragAndDropHooks.

keyboard.action: Between the row’s handle and buttons.
Starts keyboard dragging; arrows to choose the position, Enter to drop, Esc to cancel.
Moves by one position; focus stays on the moved row’s button (at the edge it moves to the other button).

accessibility: Accessible drag-and-drop from react-aria-components (handle with a localized name and drag announcements).
Move up/down buttons as a non-dragging alternative (WCAG 2.2, 2.5.7 Dragging Movements).
A role="status" region announces the new position (messages.itemMoved).
responsive: On touch, the handle and buttons have adequate targets; row content wraps.
commonMistakes: Using indexes as ids: ids must stay stable after a move.
Not persisting the order: onReorder doesn’t save anything on its own.
limits: Pointer and keyboard dragging is provided by react-aria and isn’t covered by unit tests (jsdom); tests cover buttons, announcements, states, and onReorder.
No dragging between different lists and no virtualization.
